facts.raw_span: intermittent, sharp, central chest pain with diaphoresis
pleuritic and worsened when he sat forward
denied recent viral symptoms
had not received a COVID-19 booster
stage 2 finger clubbing
sinus rhythm with benign early repolarization in the anterior leads
hemoglobin concentration of 132 g/L
low mean corpuscular volume of 75 fL
high-sensitivity troponin T of 275 ng/L
C-reactive protein was 59 mg/L
LVEF 50–55% with dyssynchronous septal motion
extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement in a mid-wall to epicardial distribution

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of intermittent, sharp, central chest pain and elevated troponin levels, combined with the CMR findings of extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement, are consistent with myocarditis.
The patient's elevated troponin levels and dyssynchronous septal motion on echocardiography suggest possible acute coronary syndrome, although the CMR findings do not support this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of pleuritic chest pain and stage 2 finger clubbing, although not specific, could be consistent with pericarditis, but the CMR findings do not support this diagnosis.
The patient's elevated C-reactive protein levels and CMR findings of extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement suggest an inflammatory process affecting the myocardium.

rationales.F01: Chest pain is a common symptom of myocarditis.
rationales.F02: Pleuritic chest pain can be seen in pericarditis.
rationales.F05: Finger clubbing can be associated with chronic conditions, but in this context, it may suggest an inflammatory process.
rationales.F09: Elevated troponin levels are a strong indicator of myocardial injury, which is consistent with myocarditis.
rationales.F10: Elevated C-reactive protein suggests an inflammatory process, which is consistent with myocarditis.
rationales.F11: Reduced LVEF with dyssynchronous septal motion is consistent with myocarditis.
rationales.F12: Extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement is a characteristic finding of myocarditis on cardiac MRI.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with intermittent, sharp, central chest pain, elevated troponin levels, and extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, along with the absence of significant coronary artery disease, supports the diagnosis of myocarditis.
